title: Portuguese dining, in short
body:
Lunch is the main meal, roughly noon–14:30; dinner runs later than a typical US schedule, 19:30–22:30. Tipping ~5–10% is customary in restaurants, never mandatory.

The bread, olives or cheese set on your table without being asked — the couvert — is a real charge if eaten, but Portuguese law says you're never obliged to pay for anything you didn't order: send it back and it's free.

title: Lisbon — what to eat
intro: Skip sit-down meals directly on Rua Augusta or around Praça do Comércio/Rossio — Portuguese travel press repeatedly flags that strip for inflated prices, weak quality and street touts; a block or two off the main drag does better.

items.name: Pastéis de Belém
items.how: Part of the Belém sightseeing walk, between Jerónimos and the Tower.
items.crowd_tip: The outside queue is for takeaway only — walk past it to the café entrance and you'll usually have a table in under 10 minutes, even at peak times. Quietest before 09:00 on weekdays or after 18:00 any day.
items.why: The original custard tart, baked to a secret 1837 recipe, in a 1,000+ seat historic café most visitors never realize exists past the queue.

items.name: Manteigaria
items.area: Multiple — Chiado, Time Out Market, Belém, Rossio (also 4 Porto locations)
items.price: ⚠ ≈€1.20–1.30 per tart — aggregator-sourced, not shown on the official site
items.why: A genuine multi-location alternative to Pastéis de Belém, watch them pipe and bake through an open kitchen window.

items.name: Time Out Market Lisboa
items.area: Cais do Sodré, in the historic Mercado da Ribeira building
items.crowd_tip: Go before noon for the least crowded stalls — by early afternoon most tables and lines run long. A convenient, genuinely touristy food hall, not where Lisboetas eat day to day.
items.why: 26 stalls and 8 bars under one roof — the operator's own site calls it 'one of Portugal's most popular tourist attractions,' so go in with that expectation rather than looking for a hidden gem.

items.name: A Ginjinha do Rossio
items.price: ⚠ ≈€1.50 per shot — no official site exists for this stall; price is aggregator-sourced only, confirm on arrival
items.why: A standing-room-only cherry liqueur stall since 1840 — cheap, fast, and a genuine Lisbon tradition.

items.name: Mercado do Bolhão
items.hours: Market stalls Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00, Sat 08:00–18:00; in-market restaurants Mon–Sat 08:00–24:00; closed Sun/holidays
items.why: Porto's historic market, reopened after a multi-year renovation — a market breakfast here beats a hotel one.

items.name: Café Santiago
items.price: ≈€8.50–10 (unconfirmed — not shown on the official page)
items.why: Serving francesinha — Porto's belt-testing sandwich under melted cheese and beer sauce — since 1959, self-billed among the '50 best sandwiches in the world.'

title: Vila Nova de Gaia — port wine cellars

items.name: Sandeman
items.why: The most straightforward cellar tour to book, with a range of tasting depths.

items.name: Taylor's
items.why: A self-guided audio tour in 13 languages, including 3 wines — good if a fixed tour time doesn't fit the day.
